reason: The check families are the contract's own vocabulary (decision 23 of the frameworks plan); three of them are named after the UI toolkit whose files they read.
The craft floor is a markup-css and react-like family check: it reads markup and CSS by their extensions. The backend sends it only for those families.
The detector is a markup-css and react-like family check, for the same reason.
Web sketches are React with Tailwind in the sandbox (decision 14), so the files the backend sends for one are named by those extensions.

The native floor is the flutter, swiftui and compose families' check (decision 23): it reads each toolkit's source files and names its buttons, so it names them. The backend sends it only for those families.
